repository.name: rclone

issue.body:
A `--max-depth` argument for the `ls` command would be nice.  It would work like `find`'s `-maxdepth` flag.

Sometimes I only want to see the files in the very top level of my dropbox.  I don't want to list ALL files in my dropbox account.

It would kind of be similar to the `lsd` command, but more flexible.

issue.title: Implement `--low-level-retries` flag

repository.description: "rsync for cloud storage" - Google Drive, S3, Dropbox, Backblaze B2, One Drive, Swift, Hubic, Wasabi, Google Cloud Storage, Azure Blob, Azure Files, Yandex Files

issue.body:
Hi,

I'm using rclone on raspberrypi to sync data on external HDD to amazon cloud. Below is the commend I'm using but the number of retries is always 10 even with the retries=1 set.

_Command:_
rclone --retries=1 sync /media/dir300/UseMe/ amzcld:UseMe/

_Log:_
2015/12/28 19:50:52 PhotosLibrary/Photos Library 9.55.20 PM.photoslibrary/Masters/2013/07/31/20130731-215027/DSC04098.JPG: Received error: HTTP code 409: "409 Conflict", reponse body: {"logref":"35dbb896-adc6-11e5-b1bb-7f2eb97d1295","message":"Node with the name dsc04098.jpg already exists under parentId dxrkTC5BTaudD71iJBhbtQ conflicting NodeId: 4vLN4NlkRDSTgd62sfbWFw","code":"NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS","info":{"nodeId":"4vLN4NlkRDSTgd62sfbWFw"}}
 **\- retrying 4/10**
2015/12/28 19:51:12

body:
Thanks for posting the errors.  Those look like winsock errors, ie your machine's TCP stack complaining that it couldn't connect.

https://www.nsoftware.com/kb/xml/07240801.rst

As for what causes it - it might be Amazon, your ISP, your router/firewall it is difficult to know.

rclone shouldn't go mad at this point, it should just carry on so there may be something which needs tweaking.  If you can get me a log of it going wrong that would be super helpful.

....

I realise I didn't do a good job of answering your original question, so I shall now!

> When uploading 100,000 or more files rclone will often get stuck trying to read the ls list of files from ACD.
> This will result in a large number of errors that say "file with this name already exists" because it will not find the file then it will add it to the list of files to upload then when it's time to upload it'll find it already existed.

Is that 100,000 files in one directory? Or 100,000 files spread out over many directories?

> Even worse this will often result in the checks portion of rclone getting stuck, literally forever, for some files. This means that when I want to sync 100,000-1,000,000 files or so to ACD I simply can't

I'm not sure why it gets stuck - is there anything in the log?

> I don't blame rclone, it's probably all ACD's fault, but I am wondering if anything could be done to help this out? perhaps rclone could save a ls from acd? allowing rclone some command to generate a full ls? allowing the user to run it a few times? to make sure they have a good ls? then start the sync using that locally stored ls? I don't know...

I've certainly considered this - see #180 

> I started just uploading large 7z files of my largest folders instead.
> 
> another sub issue here is thusly, if remote:E:\ contains let's say 10subfolders and those 10subfolders contain 1,000,000 files... and I want to upload a single file directly to "remote:E" instead of just confirming that file isn't one of the ten things in the root directory it will demand to check all 1,000,000 files (or well maybe not "check" but the ls command will be for all subdirectories)... this has resulted in me wanting to upload to "remote:incoming" then use ACD's shitty website to move the file back to "remote:E"...

That is a problem I've known about for a while #8.  I haven't thought of a satisfactory solution though - for syncing lots of files it is much faster to list the remote, but for syncing just a few it is faster not to - how can we tell which to use?  Maybe I could add in a command line flag `--no-traverse` or something like that.?

Note that sync always has to traverse the remote file system.

> ideally the ls rclone runs from ACD would only check subdirectories it needs to? this would speed things up a lot especially because ACD's response to ls is very buggy.

The error I posted above appears unrelated to the error I described in this thread. I've gotten the rclone operation stuck again though. Made 30,000checks, then spent 2hours stuck on the same four small image files making no progress, the verbose log file is 80megabytes do you want to take a look at it?

What seems to be happening is it gives me the same file with that name already exists error (error 409) endlessly for all time.... My guess is that somehow ACD's list is faulty and leaves a file out, so rclone tries to upload a new copy...then it finds the copy already exists... it retries the upload ten times listing 1/10 2/10 3/10...etc then it tries the 10th time retry 10/10 then... it tries again endlessly for all time :-/

Maybe after ten 409 errors in a row a new list needs to be asked for from ACD? I don't really know programming.

80 megabytes is too big for an email but if I edit out 29,000 perfectly fine checks I should be able to get the filesize down and email you the log.  The edited portion I guess has the error that matters is only 27kilobytes and I emailed it to you.

I think that winsock error was just a random error that happened due to my internet and rclone handled it fine.  I only posted it because it was the first error I found going through the verbose log. This 409 issue definitely seems like the real problem though after seeing the program get stuck in an infinite loop for 2hours right after the 409.
edit: another option might be to just skip those files entirely after ten failed retries? anything that breaks this infinite loop.

I have seen the 409 issue in the integration tests too.  The integration tests used to pass perfectly every time with ACD, and now they are more like 50/50, with 409 error and complete stall, which sounds very much like the same symptoms.

I'm not 100% convinced this is an rclone issue rather than just ACD being overloaded, but we'll try to get to the bottom of the problem and fix it or work around.

Oh I agree it's a problem on ACD's end but rclone could hopefully be rewritten to get around this issue. If I ctrl-c rclone and start a new similar command rclone and ACD will instantly start working on it.  It seems like maybe ACD is overloaded for a minute or two and then rclone gets stuck in an infinite loop so that even if ACD gets unclogged rclone stays in it's infinite loop forever until I force close it.

Maybe if there was a way to make it so that on any 409 error if you set the right option/flag rclone would overwrite the file? I wouldn't mind 1% of my files being wastefully uploaded and overwritten as a result of a bug on ACD's end.  
Or maybe after 10 409's in a row rclone could just skip those files entirely and at the end count them as errors? Right now it seems to just try the same 409'ing files endlessly until the error goes away, which it never will because the file exists remotely?.   

A work around I haven't tried yet but probably should, is to delete the remote copy of the 409'ing files via another method/program and then see if rclone can just upload new copies of the files letting it continue on checking the rest of the files.  If this workaround worked I could ask rclone to sync a million files once a month, and if rclone got stuck in an infinite loop I might be able to check on it once a day to manually unstick it? That might be better than what my current best solution is now.  Which is to just keep uploading my local harddrive contents to new remote folders endlessly because as long as the target folder on the cloud is empty there can be no 409 errors and so there can be no 409 infinite loop bug.

I agree 100% with you.  rclone isn't supposed to hang indefinitely - at most it is supposed to hack for `--timeout` so something is up there.

Hopefully we'll work something out for this soon!
Sorry for the noobish question, but how do I tell bash (in OS X) to write rclone's verbose log to a text file so I can share it? It's too long to just copy and paste.

All important data is backing up, so I'm reporting this in case it is helpful to the developers, not for support particularly.  This is the log output from the ACD transfers

2016/01/04 04:57:58 CLASSICAL/The Sound of Everest/Front.jpg: Failed to copy: HTTP code 409: "409 Conflict", reponse body: {"logref":"a2727a0f-b2c9-11e5-8d39-fd0c5bf37a35","message":"Node with the name front.jpg already exists under parentId F27gnDnvTS6p19bp6hu8Tw conflicting NodeId: TZ2Z86TpQq6RUEG0KOCZ8A","code":"NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS","info":{"nodeId":"TZ2Z86TpQq6RUEG0KOCZ8A"}}
2016/01/04 04:57:58 Amazon cloud drive root 'Music': Not deleting files as there were IO errors
2016/01/04 04:57:58 Attempt 3/3 failed with 1 errors

There can be dozens of these sometimes, all caused usually by a small handful of files.

This issue has completely fixed itself for me as of Sunday. There was about a week and a half where I couldn't back up my hard drive to ACD, at all—now it's working again perfectly. I guess Amazon reverted/fixed whatever had changed on their backend.

yes! me too! ACD is sync'ing flawlessly and checking quickly without errors!

it'd still be nice for rclone to handle BAD cloud service performance more robustly though by fixing this issue even if it not currently effecting me anymore.

I'd like to fix the getting stuck issue.  Interestingly I still see it with the integration tests so I've got something to work on!

eg

```
cd fs
go test -v -remote TestAmazonCloudDrive:
```

shows the problem quite regularly.
Amazon and Google are competitors in the space, so I figure Amazon may not be excessively keen to support the Go language.  Pretty sure NCW will figure it out, whatever it is.  :)

My problem may have been something to do with case sensitivity.  The remote had a file called 'Front.JPG' and the local a file called 'Front.jpg' and the sync would fail.  I manually deleted the remote file, and now ACD sync completes with no errors.
@isaiah36 that will certainly stop the sync completing - sounds like ACD is having a good day if that was the only problem!
